title: Stop Posting the Rooftop Pool: Show Buyers the Unit Instead
seoTitle: Stop Posting the Rooftop Pool (Real Estate Marketing)
description: Most condo launches post the same rooftop pool at sunset. Learn why buyers ignore it and what to show instead: the bedroom, the light, the sofa view.
answer: Stop leading your condo marketing with the rooftop pool. Nearly every new development posts the same pool at sunset, and nobody buys a unit for a pool that belongs to everyone. People buy the bedroom, the kitchen and the window they will live with every day. Show the real unit, its light and its view, because that is what buyers save.
keywords: show the unit not the amenity
body:
Try a quick test. Search for new developments, pick one, and scroll through the first ten you find. I am willing to bet that nine of them show exactly the same thing: a rooftop pool at sunset. The water, the skyline, the warm light. It looks great, and it does almost nothing to sell a unit.

## Why the rooftop pool does not sell condos

Nobody buys the pool. The pool belongs to everyone in the building. It is shared, it is the same for the buyer on the third floor and the buyer on the thirtieth, and every competing project has one that looks almost identical in a render.

When every launch posts the same amenity, the amenity stops being a reason to choose you. It becomes background noise.

## What buyers actually pay for

People buy a bedroom. A kitchen. A window. They pay for the part of the building they will live in every single day, not the part they might visit on a weekend.

And that is exactly the part nobody shows. Buyers scroll past pool after pool and still have no idea what their own home will feel like.

## What to show instead

Let people see their unit, not just the amenity. A few examples of content that works:

- **The morning light** in a one-bedroom on a lower floor.
- **The view from the sofa**, not the view from the roof.
- **The difference between units**, such as the corner unit compared with a unit in the center of the floor.

These are specific and honest. They answer the question every buyer is quietly asking: what will my home actually be like?

## Why unit content gets saved

The information people save is the information they can picture themselves in. A rooftop pool is a nice picture of someone else's lifestyle. A real bedroom with real morning light is a picture of the buyer's own life.

That is the content that gets saved, shared with a partner and brought up again when it is time to decide.

## A simple rule for your next post

Before you publish, ask one question: is this the amenity or the unit? If it is the pool again, swap it for a bedroom, a window or the view from the sofa. Show the part people live in, and you give them a reason to choose your building over the nine others posting the same sunset.
takeaways: Most new developments post the same rooftop pool at sunset, so it no longer sets anyone apart.
Nobody buys a unit for the pool, because the pool belongs to everyone in the building.
Buyers pay for the bedroom, the kitchen and the window they live with every day.
Show the morning light, the view from the sofa and the difference between units.
People save content they can picture themselves in, so unit content outperforms amenity content.
faq: What should I post to market a new condo development?
Show the units themselves: the light in a specific bedroom, the view from the sofa and how a corner unit differs from a center unit. Buyers relate to the space they will live in.
Amenities help, but they rarely decide a purchase on their own. Every competing building has similar amenities, and buyers choose based on the unit they will live in.
Why does presale marketing content look the same everywhere?
Most launches lead with the same rendered amenities, such as a rooftop pool at sunset, so the content blends together and gives buyers no reason to choose one project.
